verses.1:1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ: Grace and peace to you.
verses.1:2: We give thanks to God at all times for all of you, making mention of you in our prayers, unceasingly
verses.1:3: calling to mind your work of faith, your labor of love, and your endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ in the presence of our God and Father,
verses.1:4: knowing, brethren beloved by God, your election,
verses.1:5: because our gospel did not come to you in word alone, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and in abundant assurance, just as you know what manner of men we proved to be among you for your sake.
verses.1:6: And you yourselves became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word amid great affliction with the joy of the Holy Spirit,
verses.1:7: so that you became patterns to all who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.
verses.1:8: For from you the word of the Lord has resounded, not only in Macedonia and Achaia, but in every place your faith toward God has gone forth, so that we have no need to speak anything.
verses.1:9: For they themselves declare concerning us what manner of entrance we had to you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve a living and true God,
verses.1:10: and to await His Son from the heavens, whom He raised from the dead—Jesus, who rescues us from the coming wrath.
verses.2:1: For you yourselves know, brethren, that our entrance to you has not proved in vain,
verses.2:2: but though we had previously suffered and been shamefully mistreated at Philippi, just as you know, we grew bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God amid great conflict.
verses.2:3: For our exhortation does not arise from error, nor from impurity, nor in guile,
verses.2:4: but just as we have been tested and approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak—not as pleasing men, but God, who examines our hearts.
verses.2:5: For at no time did we come with speech of flattery, just as you know, nor with a pretext for covetousness—God is witness—
verses.2:6: nor seeking glory from men, neither from you nor from others,
verses.2:7: though we could have made demands as apostles of Christ. Yet we became infants in your midst, as a nursing mother cherishes her own children;
verses.2:8: thus, yearning affectionately for you, we were delighted to impart to you not only the gospel of God, but also our very own souls, because you had become dearly beloved to us.
verses.2:9: For you remember, brethren, our toil and hardship: working night and day, so as not to burden any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
verses.2:10: You are witnesses, and so is God, how devoutly, righteously, and blamelessly we conducted ourselves toward you who believe,
verses.2:11: just as you know how we dealt with each one of you, as a father does his own children,
verses.2:12: exhorting you, encouraging you, and solemnly charging you to walk worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.
verses.2:13: And for this reason we also give thanks to God unceasingly, that when you received the word of God which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men, but as it truly is, the word of God, which is also at work in you who believe.
verses.2:14: For you became imitators, brethren, of the churches of God in Judea that are in Christ Jesus, because you yourselves also suffered the same things from your own countrymen, just as they did from the Jews,
verses.2:15: who put to death both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and drove us out; they do not please God, and are opposed to all men,
verses.2:16: hindering us from speaking to the Gentiles that they might be saved, so as to fill up the measure of their sins at all times. But wrath has overtaken them to the uttermost.
verses.2:17: But we, brethren, having been torn away from you for a brief season—in presence, not in heart—strove all the more earnestly to see your face with great longing.
verses.2:18: For we desired to come to you—I, Paul, both once and twice—yet Satan hindered us.
verses.2:19: For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting—is it not even you—before our Lord Jesus at His coming?
verses.2:20: For you are our glory and our joy.
verses.3:1: Therefore, when we could bear it no longer, we were willing to be left behind in Athens alone,
verses.3:2: and we sent Timothy, our brother and minister of God in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen and encourage you concerning your faith,
verses.3:3: so that no one might be unsettled amid these afflictions. For you yourselves know that we are appointed for this.
verses.3:4: For indeed, when we were with you, we kept telling you beforehand that we were about to suffer affliction, just as it came to pass, and you know.
verses.3:5: For this reason, when I too could bear it no longer, I sent to learn of your faith, lest somehow the tempter had tempted you, and our labor should prove in vain.
verses.3:6: But now that Timothy has come to us from you, and has brought us good tidings of your faith and love, and that you always keep a kindly remembrance of us, longing to see us just as we also long to see you,
verses.3:7: for this reason we were comforted, brethren, over you in all our distress and affliction through your faith,
verses.3:8: for now we live, if you stand steadfast in the Lord.
verses.3:9: For what thanksgiving can we render in return to God concerning you, for all the joy with which we rejoice on your account before our God,
verses.3:10: night and day praying beyond measure that we may see your face and make complete what is lacking in your faith?
verses.3:11: Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus, direct our path to you.
verses.3:12: And may the Lord cause you to increase and overflow in love toward one another and toward all, just as we also do toward you,
verses.3:13: so that He may strengthen your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His holy ones.
verses.4:1: Finally then, brethren, we ask and exhort you in the Lord Jesus, that as you received from us how you ought to walk and to please God—just as indeed you are walking—you would abound still more.
verses.4:2: For you know what commands we delivered to you through the Lord Jesus.
verses.4:3: For this is God's will, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality,
verses.4:4: that every one of you know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor,
verses.4:5: not in passionate lust, even as the Gentiles who do not know God,
verses.4:6: that no one transgress and defraud his brother in this matter, because the Lord is an avenger concerning all these things, just as we also told you beforehand and solemnly testified.
verses.4:7: For God did not call us for uncleanness, but in sanctification.
verses.4:8: Consequently, he who rejects this does not reject man, but God, who also gives His Holy Spirit to you.
verses.4:9: Now concerning brotherly love, you have no need that we write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another;
verses.4:10: for indeed you practice it toward all the brethren throughout all Macedonia. Yet we exhort you, brethren, to abound still more,
verses.4:11: and to make it your ambition to live quietly, to attend to your own affairs, and to labor with your own hands, just as we commanded you,
verses.4:12: so that you may walk honorably toward those who are outside, and be in need of nothing.
verses.4:13: Now we do not want you to be unaware, brethren, concerning those who sleep, lest you sorrow even as the rest do, who have no hope.
verses.4:14: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God, through Jesus, will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep.
verses.4:15: For this we say to you by a word of the Lord, that we who live, who remain until the coming of the Lord, shall by no means precede those who have fallen asleep.
verses.4:16: For the Lord Himself, with a shout of command, with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God, shall descend from heaven; and the dead in Christ shall rise first.
verses.4:17: Then we who live, who remain, shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air; and so we shall always be with the Lord.
verses.4:18: So then, comfort one another with these words.
verses.5:1: Now concerning the times and the seasons, brethren, you have no need for anything to be written to you,
verses.5:2: for you yourselves know full well that the day of the Lord comes just as a thief in the night.
verses.5:3: When they say, "Peace and security!" then sudden destruction comes upon them, as birth pangs upon a woman with child; and they shall by no means escape.
verses.5:4: Yet you, brethren, are not in darkness, that the day should overtake you like a thief.
verses.5:5: For all of you are sons of light and sons of day; we are not of the night, nor of darkness.
verses.5:6: So then, let us not sleep as the rest do, but let us keep watch and be sober.
verses.5:7: For those who sleep, sleep by night, and those who become drunk are drunk by night.
verses.5:8: Yet as those who are of the day, let us be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation.
verses.5:9: For God did not appoint us for wrath, but for the obtaining of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.5:10: who died on our behalf, so that whether we are awake or sleep, we may live together with Him.
verses.5:11: Therefore comfort one another and build each other up, just as indeed you are doing.
verses.5:12: Now we ask you, brethren, to acknowledge those who labor among you, who preside over you in the Lord and admonish you,
verses.5:13: and to esteem them beyond measure in love on account of their work. Live in peace among yourselves.
verses.5:14: And we exhort you, brethren: admonish the disorderly, console the fainthearted, sustain the weak, be longsuffering toward all.
verses.5:15: See to it that no one repays evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue what is good, both toward one another and toward all.
verses.5:18: in everything give thanks; for this is God's will in Christ Jesus concerning you.
verses.5:20: do not treat prophecies with contempt;
verses.5:21: but test all things; hold fast to what is good;
verses.5:22: refrain from every kind of evil.
verses.5:23: Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you wholly, and may your entire spirit and soul and body be preserved without blame at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.5:24: Faithful is He who calls you, who will also perform it.
verses.5:26: Salute all the brethren with a holy kiss.
verses.5:27: I put you under oath by the Lord that this epistle be read to all the brethren.
verses.5:28: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

notes.1:1: The critical Greek text preserves the shorter greeting without the later scribal expansion 'from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.'
notes.1:4: The Greek syntax connects 'by God' directly with 'beloved' ('brethren beloved by God') rather than with 'your election.'
notes.1:7: The critical text reads the plural 'patterns' (τύπους), whereas some manuscripts read the singular 'pattern' (τύπον).
notes.2:7: The Greek critical text reads 'infants' (νήπιοι), differing by one letter from the manuscript variant 'gentle' (ἤπιοι). The phrase rendered 'made demands' literally means 'to be in weight,' conveying either asserting apostolic authority or imposing a financial burden.
notes.2:16: The Greek phrase εἰς τέλος ('to the uttermost') is variously interpreted as 'completely,' 'at last,' or 'forever.'
notes.2:19: The Greek term παρουσία ('coming') denotes a royal arrival or personal presence.
notes.3:2: The Greek critical text reads 'minister of God' (διάκονον τοῦ θεοῦ); other manuscripts read 'coworker of God' or combine both titles.
notes.3:11: In Greek, the optative verb 'direct' is singular despite having a compound subject ('our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus'), emphasizing their unity of action.
notes.3:13: The Greek phrase τῶν ἁγίων αὐτοῦ ('His holy ones') may refer to angels (as in Zechariah 14:5), to redeemed believers, or to both together.
notes.4:4: The Greek phrase rendered "possess his own vessel" is debated, understood either as exercising self-control over one's own body or as taking and living with one's own wife in holiness.
notes.4:8: The critical Greek text reads the present participle "gives" and "to you," emphasizing God's ongoing gift of the Spirit, whereas some later manuscripts read the past tense "has given" and "to us."
notes.4:14: In Greek, "through Jesus" stands between "those who have fallen asleep" and "will bring," and may modify either God's act of bringing them or those who have fallen asleep in Jesus.
notes.5:10: Here Paul adapts the imagery of verses 6-7 to echo 4:13-17, using "awake" and "sleep" to refer to whether believers are still alive or have died when Christ returns.
notes.5:14: The Greek term rendered "the disorderly" denotes those living out of step with apostolic order, in this context particularly those neglecting honest labor (cf. 4:11).
notes.5:22: The Greek noun eidos here carries the sense of "kind" or "form" (every sort of evil), though it has also been traditionally rendered "appearance."
notes.5:27: Following the critical Greek text, which reads "all the brethren"; some later manuscripts add "holy" before "brethren."
